title: API contract evolution - architecture review log
content:
Meeting: Architecture review — API contract evolution and graceful migration
Date: 2025-07-11 10:00-11:30 PT
Location: Zoom + #platform-architecture channel
Attendees: Priya (owner, facilitator), Miguel, Aisha, Daniel, Elliot, Ravi, and notes from product (Lena) joined for last 20m
Purpose: Review RFC-2025-07 proposing a platform-wide, minimal-invasive versioning strategy for service/api contracts (control-plane and runtime APIs) to support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments without service-downtime or cross-version regressions.

Summary of problem:
- We have diverging client expectations across hosted API (external customers), Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) installs. Each has different upgrade windows and network constraints.
- Current approach has ad-hoc compatibility shims and rollout scripts in multiple repos; this increases developer cognitive load and causes occasional 500s when clients call newer features against older control planes.
- Goal: Define a clear, operationally-safe contract/versioning model that:
  * Enables additive changes without breaking older clients (backwards compatibility),
  * Allows opt-in breaking changes with controlled rollout (canary + migration window),
  * Minimizes runtime branching inside the serving runtime, and
  * Supports private deployments with delayed upgrade cadence.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Non-goal: Rewriting all client SDKs; changes should be server-first with SDK updates following.
- Must not require synchronous full-cluster restarts (where possible) for Hosted.
- Private deployments may need documented manual steps for migration; automation is desired but out-of-scope for initial phase.

Reviewed proposals (high level):
1) Strict semantic versioning (major.minor.patch) with content negotiation header (Accept-API-Version) per request
   - Pros: Explicit version selection, clear server-side branching, immediate compatibility control.
   - Cons: Adds request-level overhead, complicates routing & caching (cache keys need version), customers must opt-in per request or rely on SDKs to set header. Not friendly for streaming responses and function-calls where headers are not always propagated.

2) Backwards-compatible feature flags encoded in payload + feature-gates in control plane
   - Pros: Low-change on request surface (no separate version header), easier for gradual opt-in, good for additive features.
   - Cons: Hard to reason about for breaking changes, proliferating flags tend to linger, increases payload complexity and testing matrix.

3) Dual-mode runtime with negotiation + compatibility layer: server advertises supported capability set on session establish; clients receive a session token pinned to capabilities. Requests reference session token; runtime routes to matched implementation.
   - Pros: Session-pinning reduces per-request overhead, supports streaming and long-lived conversations, aligns with conversation routing and KV cache semantics. Works well with conversation-level feature gating.
   - Cons: Session migration needed on upgrade, more complex server-side session management, potential increase in stateful routing surface.

4) API evolution via opt-in ‘preview’ feature paths plus a graceful fallback mechanism. Preview endpoints are under /v-next/ or query param ?preview=featureX. Production clients default to stable endpoints; the control plane can map preview -> stable on a per-tenant basis during rollout.
   - Pros: Clear separation of preview code paths, easy measurement, safe default.
   - Cons: Endpoint proliferation and documentation burden; private deployments may not advertise preview paths initially.

Consensus and synthesis:
- Team leaned towards a hybrid of (3) and (4): session-capability negotiation (to minimize per-request headers) with explicit preview endpoints/workflows for breaking changes.
- Key idea: Establish a lightweight Session Capability Token (SCT) at the start of a conversation/stream. SCT encodes the minimal capability set (list of stable features) and an expiry. Requests referencing SCT are implicitly bound to that capability set. For preview/breaking changes we require explicit opt-in via preview endpoints that return a new SCT.

Operational model proposed:
- Control plane changes: implement capability registry (Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-API-CONTRACTS-102). Each capability has: id, stable|preview flag, minimum server version, rollout notes, telemetry keys.
- Runtime behavior:
  * On session create (POST /sessions), server returns SCT (JWT-like but short lived) listing capabilities.
  * Serving runtime validates SCT and routes to the correct model variant/kernel path.
  * For older runtimes that don’t understand SCT, control-plane will return stable-only SCT (compat mode).
- Caching: Cache keys must include capability-hash (derived from SCT) to avoid cross-version cache poisoning.
- Telemetry: Tag traces and token-cost records with capability-id(s) and SCT hash; ensure analytics can filter by preview usage.

Rollout strategy and migration plan:
- Phase 0 (pilot): Implement capability registry and SCT issuance in control plane, no runtime branching. Feature: “response-structured-output-v1” additive capability. Deploy to staging and internal dogfood tenants. (Owner: Aisha — Jira PLAT-8472)
- Phase 1 (canary): Serve preview capability to a small % of hosted traffic via preview endpoints returning preview-SCT. Monitor error-rate, latency delta, and model-quality metrics for 2 weeks. (Owner: Miguel)
- Phase 2 (gradual stable): If stable, mark capability stable in registry; control-plane can start issuing stable-SCTs by default. SDKs will be updated to use session creation flow. Communicate migration docs for Dedicated and Private customers with clear rollback steps. (Owner: Daniel + Solutions Eng)
- Phase 3 (private deployments): Publish a migration playbook and a CLI helper for SCT negotiation and server capability introspection. Private installs can run air-gapped migration scripts to add new capabilities. (Owner: Ravi)

Decisions (explicit):
- Adopt SCT-based session negotiation as primary mechanism (decision pending final perf bench).
- Keep preview endpoints for opt-in breaking changes; preview endpoints must always return a new SCT.
- SDKs will be updated to manage session lifecycle and prefer session-bound calls.
- Control-plane must provide a capability-compatibility matrix per release.

Open questions / action items from meeting: (owners and due dates)
- Perf bench: Measure SCT overhead (token validation & capability-hash cache impact) vs header-based versioning. (Elliot, due 2025-07-18)
- Security review: SCT encoding and expiry, replay risk, and KMS usage for signing tokens. (Security: Nikhil, due 2025-07-22)
- SDK changes: Draft SDK session helper API, default fallback behavior when server returns stable-only SCT. (DX team: Lena + Miguel, due 2025-07-25)
- Docs: Capability registry spec and public migration guide for Dedicated/Private. (Priya + Daniel, due 2025-07-20)
- Backfill tests: Create unit/integration test plan that simulates mixed capabilities and cache-hit correctness. (QA: Aisha, due 2025-07-27)
- Jira epic: Create migration epic with tickets for CP, runtime, SDKs, docs, telemetry. Linked: JIRA-PLAT-8472 (Priya)

Risks discussed:
- Stateful session tokens add complexity to routing and state transfer in autoscaling events. Need to ensure session affinity or token-agnostic routing fallback.
- Capacity planning: preview usage could increase model variant counts and memory pressure. Monitoring & quota gating required.
- Private deployments with longer upgrade windows will require clear backward compatibility guarantees; otherwise customers may run older runtime that cannot enforce new capability constraints.

Mitigations:
- Provide automatic session re-issuance and migration hooks in control-plane for rolling upgrades.
- Capacity: enforce tenant-level preview quotas and inventory model-variant load before broad rollouts.
- Provide an explicit ‘compat-mode’ in control-plane for older runtime detection; compatibility matrix will indicate when older runtimes will no longer be issued certain capabilities.

Notes & technical observations from runtime owners:
- Elliot: token validation should be cheap; prefer HMAC-signed SCTs with key rotation support, avoid heavyweight JOSE libraries unless needed for cross-platform. Suggest caching validated token -> capability-hash in local process for X minutes.
- Daniel: session-pin reduces per-request branching and helps KV cache correctness, but time-window for SCT expiry is critical — too short leads to frequent re-creation; too long blocks migration. Recommend 24h default with a migration override.
- Miguel: Preview endpoints should include a tooling header that signals to the control plane why the preview was requested (sdk-preview, admin-toggle, ci-test) to help analytics.
- Aisha: existing e2e tests must be expanded to run mixed capability scenarios; add a simulation harness that can replay user conversations across capability transitions.

Follow-ups / next meeting:
- Weekly sync: Tuesdays 10:00 PT, same channel. Next meeting 2025-07-15 to review perf bench results and initial SCT PoC logs (Elliot + Aisha).
- Priya will circulate a lightweight decision doc summarizing choices, with a clear rollback plan for the first capability pilot.

Appendix (short examples):
- Example session create flow:
  Request: POST /sessions {"model":"redwood-2-small","client_id":"cli-abc"} -> Response {"session_id":"s-123","sct":"eyJhb...","capabilities":["structured-output-v1","prefix-cache-v2"]}
- Cache key example: cache_key = sha256(model + prompt_prefix + sct_hash)
- Minimal capability registry entry: "structured-output-v1" -> {min_server: 2025.07.1, public: false, telemetry: [cap.struct_out.v1.latency], rollout_policy: canary}

Closing:
- Tone from product: Lena emphasized the importance of clear customer comms for Dedicated & Private installs; marketing & solutions engineering involvement required early.
- Action owners please update the linked Jira epic and attach implementation notes to CONFLUENCE-PLAT-API-CONTRACTS-102.

Doc history:
- 2025-07-11 initial notes + decisions (Priya)
- 2025-07-15 updated with perf bench schedule and owners (Priya)

Notes to reviewers: Please flag any missing rollout risk vectors (billing, quota, cache invalidation), and call out any security concerns around token usage.
